body.text: Should you stay in Kaleiçi Old Town, Konyaaltı, Lara or Belek?

Choose Kaleiçi Old Town for Ottoman mansion hotels, restaurants, and walkable history; Konyaaltı for a long pebble beach with mountain views and easy city access; Lara for sandy all-inclusive resorts close to the airport; and Belek for gated golf resorts 40 minutes east. Picking the wrong zone is the single biggest mistake visitors make in Antalya.

body.text: As outlined in [GoTürkiye's Antalya guide](https://goturkiye.com/antalya/see), Kaleiçi sits inside horseshoe-shaped Hellenistic, Roman, and Ottoman walls anchored by Hadrian's Gate and the old Roman harbour. If you want to explore ancient Pamphylia and dine at neighbourhood lokantas, base yourself on the quieter southern edges of Kaleiçi or in Konyaaltı rather than locking yourself inside an all-inclusive wristband perimeter in Lara or Belek.
How many days does Antalya need?

Plan three full days to see Kaleiçi, enjoy a beach afternoon, and visit two or three major ancient cities without rushing; extend to four or five days if you want to add Olympos, Phaselis, or a boat outing along the Düden cliffs. Travellers using Antalya purely as an airport gateway to Kaş or Fethiye often regret giving the city less than 48 hours.

One crucial 2026 planning update: the [Antalya Archaeological Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3FsectionId%3DANT01%26distId%3DANT) closed in July 2025 for demolition and construction of a new museum building, and coverage from [The Türkiye Guide](https://theturkiyeguide.com/news/2026-07-09-antalya-archaeology-museum-closed-2026/) confirms it remains closed throughout 2026 with no confirmed public reopening date yet. Do not build your itinerary around its Perge sculpture halls until official reopening dates appear on muze.gov.tr; instead, visit the open Antalya Necropolis Museum or spend that half-day at Perge itself.
Which ancient cities (Perge, Aspendos, Termessos) are within an hour?

Three extraordinary ancient cities sit within 25 to 50 minutes of central Antalya: Pamphylian metropolis Perge (18 km east), intact Roman theatre Aspendos (42 km east), and mountain fortress Termessos (31 km northwest). You can easily pair Perge and Aspendos in one day, while steep, forested Termessos deserves its own half-day.

items: [Perge](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=PRG01&DistId=PRG) (25 min east): Features twin Hellenistic gate towers, a 12,000-seat stadium, Roman baths, and a colonnaded street split by a central water channel. Note that Perge's theatre is temporarily closed for restoration per muze.gov.tr.

[Aspendos](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=ASP01&DistId=ASP) (45 min east): Home to the best-preserved Roman theatre in the Mediterranean (12,000–15,000 capacity, built under Marcus Aurelius) plus a dramatic 1-kilometre stone aqueduct stretching across the plain. Foreign visitor entry is €15.

[Termessos](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=TRM&SectionId=TRM02) (40–45 min northwest): Perched above 1,000 metres in Güllük Dağı National Park, this Pisidian stronghold resisted Alexander the Great in 333 BC. Expect a steep 25-minute rocky trail from the upper car park to the cliffside theatre—wear hiking shoes and bring water.

body.text: Yes—spring (April–May) and autumn (late September–early November) are dramatically better than July and August for sightseeing, hiking, and comfortable beach days. Even winter (December–February) stays mild, with daytime highs averaging 15–18°C according to [Weather Spark's Antalya climate data](https://weatherspark.com/y/96456/Average-Weather-in-Antalya-Turkey-Year-Round), making it one of Europe's easiest winter sun escapes.

In July and August, afternoon heat frequently tops 35–40°C with heavy coastal humidity, turning unshaded ruins like Perge into an oven after 10:30. By contrast, October delivers 25–28°C air temperatures and sea water still above 22°C, as noted in [GoTürkiye's 48-hour Antalya guide](https://goturkiye.com/antalya/48-hours). Winter brings intermittent heavy rain showers followed by bright blue skies—ideal for quiet Kaleiçi walks, empty ruins, and even morning skiing at Saklıkent above town before lunch by the harbour.

Connecting Antalya west along the Turquoise Coast toward [Fethiye and Ölüdeniz](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/fethiye-oludeniz-guide) or inland to Cappadocia requires careful pacing so you do not lose whole days to coastal switchbacks. faq.q: How do you get from Antalya Airport (AYT) to Kaleiçi Old Town?
faq.a: The AntRay T1A tram runs directly from Antalya Airport's domestic and international terminals to İsmetpaşa or Muratpaşa stops beside Kaleiçi in about 35 minutes; taxis take 25–30 minutes depending on traffic.

faq.q: Is the Antalya Archaeological Museum open in 2026?
faq.a: No. The museum closed on 16 July 2025 for demolition and rebuilding of a new facility and remains closed throughout 2026. Check muze.gov.tr before travelling for official reopening announcements.

faq.q: Can you visit Perge, Aspendos, and Termessos in the same day?
faq.a: Technically possible with an early start and a private driver, but exhausting because Termessos sits northwest in the mountains while Perge and Aspendos lie east on the coastal plain. Splitting them across two half-days is far more enjoyable.

faq.q: Is Konyaaltı Beach sand or pebble?
faq.a: Konyaaltı is a smooth grey pebble beach backed by a modern promenade of parks, cafés, and bike lanes. If you strictly want soft sand, head east to Lara Beach or west to Patara.

faq.q: Do you need a rental car in Antalya?
faq.a: Not if you are staying in Kaleiçi or Konyaaltı and visiting city sights, as trams and taxis work well. Rent a car—or hire a private driver—for the days you visit Termessos, Aspendos, or drive west toward Kaş.

faq.q: Can you swim in Antalya in November?
faq.a: Many visitors still swim in early November when sea temperatures hover around 21–22°C on sunny afternoons, though by late November most people switch to coastal walks and ancient-site touring.
